_ui.no_range: There was no range to compare this number with, so we can't say whether it is high or low. Ask your doctor what it means for you.

_generic.measures: This test is part of your {panel} check. Your doctor uses it together with your other results.

low.means: Your result is below the range on your report.
causes: Many everyday things can change this value
Timing of the test and recent meals can matter
ask: What could explain this result?
Should this test be repeated?
Is there anything I should change before the next test?

high.means: Your result is above the range on your report.
causes: Many everyday things can change this value
Timing of the test and recent meals can matter
ask: What could explain this result?
Should this test be repeated?
Is there anything I should change before the next test?

normal.means: Your result is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should this test be checked?

HGB.measures: Haemoglobin is the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.

low.means: Your haemoglobin is below the range. This means your blood may be carrying less oxygen than usual. Only a doctor can say why it is low.
causes: Blood loss, such as heavy periods or bleeding in the gut
ask: Why might my haemoglobin be low?
Should I have my iron, B12 and folate checked?
Do I need a supplement or a change in diet?
When should I repeat this test?

high.means: Your haemoglobin is above the range. Your blood has more red cells or haemoglobin than usual.
causes: Not drinking enough water before the test
ask: What might cause my haemoglobin to be high?
Should I repeat the test after drinking more water?
Do I need any other tests?

normal.means: Your haemoglobin is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should I check my haemoglobin?

RBC.measures: This counts your red blood cells. These cells carry oxygen around your body.

low.means: You have fewer red blood cells than the range.
ask: Why might my red cell count be low?
Should other blood tests be done?

high.means: You have more red blood cells than the range.
ask: What might cause a high red cell count?
Should I repeat this test?

normal.means: Your red cell count is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should I check my blood count?

WBC.measures: This counts your white blood cells. These cells help your body fight infection.

low.means: You have fewer white blood cells than the range. Your body may be less able to fight germs.
causes: Problems with how the bone marrow makes cells
ask: Why might my white cell count be low?
Do I need to take extra care to avoid infections?
When should this be rechecked?

high.means: You have more white blood cells than the range. This often happens when the body is fighting something.
causes: Stress on the body, such as surgery
ask: Could I have an infection?
Do I need more tests?
When should this be rechecked?

normal.means: Your white cell count is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should I check my blood count?

PLT.measures: Platelets are tiny blood cells that help your blood clot and stop bleeding.

low.means: You have fewer platelets than the range. You may bruise or bleed more easily.
causes: A recent viral infection such as dengue
Problems with how the bone marrow makes cells
ask: Why might my platelets be low?
Should I watch for bruising or bleeding?
Do I need to stop any medicine?

high.means: You have more platelets than the range.
ask: What might raise my platelet count?
Do I need more tests?

normal.means: Your platelet count is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should I check my platelets?

MCV.measures: MCV is the average size of your red blood cells.

low.means: Your red cells are smaller than usual.
ask: Should my iron levels be checked?

high.means: Your red cells are larger than usual.
ask: Should my B12 and folate be checked?

normal.means: Your red cell size is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other blood results?

MCH.measures: MCH is the average amount of haemoglobin inside each red blood cell.

low.means: Each red cell holds less haemoglobin than usual.
ask: Should my iron levels be checked?

high.means: Each red cell holds more haemoglobin than usual, often because the cells are larger.
ask: Should my B12 and folate be checked?

normal.means: Your MCH is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other blood results?

MCHC.measures: MCHC shows how concentrated the haemoglobin is inside your red blood cells.

low.means: The haemoglobin in your red cells is less concentrated than usual.
ask: Should my iron levels be checked?

high.means: The haemoglobin in your red cells is more concentrated than usual.
ask: Should this test be repeated?

normal.means: Your MCHC is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other blood results?

NEUT.measures: Neutrophils are the most common white blood cells. They fight bacteria.

low.means: You have a smaller share of neutrophils than usual.
ask: Do I need to take extra care to avoid infections?

high.means: You have a larger share of neutrophils than usual.
ask: Could I have an infection?

normal.means: Your neutrophil share is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other blood results?

LYMPH.measures: Lymphocytes are white blood cells that fight viruses and help your immune memory.

low.means: You have a smaller share of lymphocytes than usual.
ask: What could explain this?

high.means: You have a larger share of lymphocytes than usual.
ask: Could I have a viral infection?
Should this be rechecked?

normal.means: Your lymphocyte share is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other blood results?

EOS.measures: Eosinophils are white blood cells linked to allergies and some infections.

low.means: You have a smaller share of eosinophils than usual. Doctors rarely act on this result on its own.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: You have a larger share of eosinophils than usual.
ask: Could allergies explain this?
Do I need a stool test?

normal.means: Your eosinophil share is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other blood results?

PCV.measures: PCV, also called haematocrit, is the share of your blood made up of red cells.

low.means: Red cells make up less of your blood than usual.
ask: Why might my PCV be low?

high.means: Red cells make up more of your blood than usual.
ask: Should I repeat this after drinking more water?

normal.means: Your PCV is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should I check my blood count?

TBIL.measures: Bilirubin is a yellow substance made when old red blood cells break down. The liver clears it.

low.means: Your bilirubin is below the range. Doctors rarely act on this result on its own.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your bilirubin is above the range. The liver may not be clearing it as fast as usual, or more red cells may be breaking down.
causes: A common inherited trait that raises bilirubin
ask: Why might my bilirubin be high?
Do I need a liver scan?
Should I avoid alcohol or any medicine?

normal.means: Your bilirubin is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my liver tests be checked?

DBIL.measures: Direct bilirubin is the part of bilirubin the liver has already processed.

low.means: Your direct bilirubin is below the range. Doctors rarely act on this result on its own.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your direct bilirubin is above the range. Bile may not be draining from the liver as usual.
ask: Do I need a liver or gallbladder scan?

normal.means: Your direct bilirubin is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my liver tests be checked?

AST.measures: SGOT, also called AST, is an enzyme found in the liver, heart and muscles. It leaks into the blood when these cells are stressed.

low.means: Your SGOT is below the range. Doctors rarely act on this result on its own.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your SGOT is above the range. Some liver or muscle cells may be under stress.
ask: Why might my SGOT be high?
Should I repeat this test?
Should I stop any medicine or alcohol?

normal.means: Your SGOT is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my liver tests be checked?

ALT.measures: SGPT, also called ALT, is an enzyme mostly found in the liver. When liver cells are stressed, more of it leaks into the blood.

low.means: Your SGPT is below the range. Doctors rarely act on this result on its own.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your SGPT is above the range. This suggests some liver cells may be under stress. It does not tell you why.
causes: Fat building up in the liver
Some medicines, including common pain relievers and some cholesterol medicines
A viral infection of the liver
ask: What could be raising my SGPT?
Should I have a liver ultrasound?
Could any of my medicines be affecting my liver?
When should I repeat my liver tests?

normal.means: Your SGPT is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my liver tests be checked?

ALP.measures: Alkaline phosphatase is an enzyme from the liver, bile ducts and bones.

low.means: Your ALP is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your ALP is above the range. The source can be the liver or the bones.
ask: Is this coming from my liver or my bones?
Do I need more tests?

normal.means: Your ALP is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my liver tests be checked?

ALB.measures: Albumin is the main protein in your blood. It is made by the liver and helps keep fluid inside blood vessels.

low.means: Your albumin is below the range.
ask: Why might my albumin be low?
Should I eat more protein?

high.means: Your albumin is above the range. This usually means you were low on water.
ask: Should I repeat this after drinking more water?

normal.means: Your albumin is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other results?

TP.measures: Total protein is all the protein in your blood, mainly albumin and globulins.

low.means: Your total protein is below the range.
ask: Why might my protein be low?

high.means: Your total protein is above the range.
ask: Do I need a protein test called electrophoresis?

normal.means: Your total protein is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other results?

AGR.measures: The A/G ratio compares albumin with the other blood proteins, called globulins.

low.means: You have less albumin compared with globulins than usual.
ask: What could explain my A/G ratio?

high.means: You have more albumin compared with globulins than usual.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

normal.means: Your A/G ratio is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my other results?

UREA.measures: Urea is a waste product from breaking down protein. Your kidneys remove it from the blood.

low.means: Your urea is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your urea is above the range. Your kidneys may be clearing waste more slowly, or you may be low on water.
ask: Is my kidney function changing?
Should I drink more water?

normal.means: Your urea is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my kidney tests be checked?

BUN.measures: BUN measures the nitrogen from urea in your blood. It shows how well your kidneys remove waste.

low.means: Your BUN is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your BUN is above the range.
ask: Is my kidney function changing?

normal.means: Your BUN is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my kidney tests be checked?

CREAT.measures: Creatinine is a waste product from your muscles. Your kidneys filter it out of the blood, so it shows how well they are working.

low.means: Your creatinine is below the range. This often reflects lower muscle mass.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your creatinine is above the range. Your kidneys may be filtering more slowly than usual.
causes: Some medicines, including some pain relievers
High blood pressure or high blood sugar over many years
ask: Is my kidney function changing?
Should my medicines be adjusted for my kidneys?
Do I need a urine test for protein?

normal.means: Your creatinine is within the normal range on your report.
ask: Has my creatinine changed since my last test?
How often should my kidney tests be checked?

URIC.measures: Uric acid is a waste product from breaking down certain foods. Your kidneys remove it.

low.means: Your uric acid is below the range. Doctors rarely act on this result on its own.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your uric acid is above the range. High levels can form crystals in joints.
ask: Do I need to change my diet?
Could this explain any joint pain?

normal.means: Your uric acid is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should this be checked?

EGFR.measures: eGFR is an estimate of how much blood your kidneys filter each minute. It is worked out from your creatinine, age and sex.

low.means: Your eGFR is below the range. Your kidneys may be filtering less than usual.
ask: What does my eGFR mean for my kidneys?
Should any medicines be adjusted?
When should this be rechecked?

high.means: Your eGFR is above the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

normal.means: Your eGFR is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my kidney tests be checked?

NA.measures: Sodium is a salt in your blood. It helps control water balance, nerves and muscles.

low.means: Your sodium is below the range. This can cause tiredness, confusion or falls, especially in older adults.
causes: Some water pills or other medicines
ask: Why might my sodium be low?
Could my medicines be the cause?
Should I change how much I drink?

high.means: Your sodium is above the range. This usually means your body is low on water.
ask: Should I drink more water?
When should this be rechecked?

normal.means: Your sodium is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my salts be checked?

K.measures: Potassium is a salt in your blood. It helps your nerves and muscles work, including your heart muscle.

low.means: Your potassium is below the range. Low potassium can affect muscles and heart rhythm.
ask: Why might my potassium be low?
Do I need a supplement?
Should I have an ECG?

high.means: Your potassium is above the range. High potassium can affect the rhythm of the heart, so doctors act on it quickly.
causes: A sample that was shaken or delayed, which can falsely raise the result
ask: Should this be repeated today?
Do I need an ECG?
Could any of my medicines be raising my potassium?
Should I avoid any foods or salt substitutes?

normal.means: Your potassium is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my salts be checked?

CL.measures: Chloride is a salt in your blood. It works with sodium to keep fluids balanced.

low.means: Your chloride is below the range.
ask: What could explain this?

high.means: Your chloride is above the range.
ask: What could explain this?

normal.means: Your chloride is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my salts be checked?

CA.measures: Calcium is a mineral used for bones, nerves, muscles and heart rhythm.

low.means: Your calcium is below the range.
causes: Low albumin, which can make calcium look low
ask: Should my vitamin D be checked?
Should my calcium be corrected for albumin?

high.means: Your calcium is above the range.
causes: An overactive gland in the neck called the parathyroid
Too much calcium or vitamin D supplement
ask: Should my parathyroid hormone be checked?
Should I stop any supplements?

normal.means: Your calcium is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should this be checked?

PHOS.measures: Phosphorus is a mineral that works with calcium to build bones and give cells energy.

low.means: Your phosphorus is below the range.
ask: What could explain this?

high.means: Your phosphorus is above the range.
ask: Is my kidney function affecting this?

normal.means: Your phosphorus is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should this be checked?

CHOL.measures: Total cholesterol is all the cholesterol in your blood. Cholesterol is a fat your body needs, but too much can build up in blood vessels.

low.means: Your total cholesterol is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your total cholesterol is above the recommended level.
ask: What is my overall heart risk?
Do I need medicine for cholesterol?
What diet changes would help most?

normal.means: Your total cholesterol is within the recommended range on your report.
ask: How often should my cholesterol be checked?

LDL.measures: LDL is often called 'bad' cholesterol. Over time it can build up in the walls of blood vessels.

low.means: Your LDL is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your LDL is above the recommended level. Higher LDL over many years raises the chance of blocked blood vessels.
causes: Diet high in saturated fat, such as ghee, butter and fried food
ask: What LDL level should I aim for, given my other health conditions?
Would a cholesterol medicine help me?
What diet changes would help most?
When should I recheck my lipids?

normal.means: Your LDL is within the recommended range on your report.
ask: How often should my cholesterol be checked?

HDL.measures: HDL is often called 'good' cholesterol. It helps carry extra cholesterol away from blood vessels.

low.means: Your HDL is below the recommended level. Less cholesterol is being carried away from your blood vessels.
ask: How can I raise my HDL?
What is my overall heart risk?

high.means: Your HDL is above the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

normal.means: Your HDL is within the recommended range on your report.
ask: How often should my cholesterol be checked?

TG.measures: Triglycerides are the most common type of fat in your blood. Your body stores extra calories as triglycerides.

low.means: Your triglycerides are below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your triglycerides are above the recommended level.
causes: Sweets, white rice, sugary drinks or alcohol
ask: Was I fasting long enough for this test?
What diet changes would lower my triglycerides?
Is my blood sugar affecting this?

normal.means: Your triglycerides are within the recommended range on your report.
ask: How often should my lipids be checked?

VLDL.measures: VLDL is a type of cholesterol that carries triglycerides in the blood.

low.means: Your VLDL is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your VLDL is above the range. It usually rises along with triglycerides.
ask: How can I lower my triglycerides?

normal.means: Your VLDL is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my lipids be checked?

CHOLHDL.measures: This ratio compares total cholesterol with HDL. A lower ratio is better for blood vessels.

low.means: Your ratio is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your ratio is above the recommended level. There is a lot of total cholesterol compared with 'good' HDL.
ask: What is my overall heart risk?

normal.means: Your ratio is within the recommended range on your report.
ask: How often should my lipids be checked?

TSH.measures: TSH is a signal from the brain that tells your thyroid gland how hard to work.

low.means: Your TSH is below the range. This can mean the thyroid is making more hormone than needed.
causes: Too high a dose of thyroid medicine
ask: Should my T3 and T4 be checked?
Does my thyroid dose need changing?

high.means: Your TSH is above the range. This can mean the thyroid is not making enough hormone.
causes: Too low a dose of thyroid medicine
ask: Should my T3 and T4 be checked?
Do I need thyroid medicine?

normal.means: Your TSH is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my thyroid be checked?

T3.measures: T3 is one of the two main thyroid hormones. It controls how fast your body uses energy.

low.means: Your T3 is below the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

high.means: Your T3 is above the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

normal.means: Your T3 is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my thyroid be checked?

T4.measures: T4 is the main hormone made by the thyroid gland.

low.means: Your T4 is below the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

high.means: Your T4 is above the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

normal.means: Your T4 is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my thyroid be checked?

FT3.measures: Free T3 is the active thyroid hormone that is free to work in your body.

low.means: Your free T3 is below the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

high.means: Your free T3 is above the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

normal.means: Your free T3 is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my thyroid be checked?

FT4.measures: Free T4 is the thyroid hormone that is free to work in your body.

low.means: Your free T4 is below the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

high.means: Your free T4 is above the range.
ask: How does this fit with my TSH?

normal.means: Your free T4 is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my thyroid be checked?

HBA1C.measures: HbA1c shows your average blood sugar over the past few months. Sugar sticks to red blood cells, and this test measures how much has stuck.

low.means: Your HbA1c is below the range.
causes: Some blood conditions that shorten red cell life
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your HbA1c is above the target level. Your average blood sugar over the past few months has been higher than recommended.
causes: Blood sugar that has stayed high for months
Diet high in sweets, rice or refined flour
ask: What HbA1c target is right for me?
Do I need to start or change diabetes medicine?
How often should I check my blood sugar at home?
Should my eyes, kidneys and feet be checked?

normal.means: Your HbA1c is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my HbA1c be checked?

FBS.measures: Fasting glucose is your blood sugar after not eating for at least eight hours.

low.means: Your fasting blood sugar is below the range. Very low sugar can cause shaking, sweating or confusion.
ask: Do my diabetes medicines need changing?
What should I do if I feel shaky or sweaty?

high.means: Your fasting blood sugar is above the range.
causes: The body not using insulin well
Not fasting fully before the test
ask: Should I have an HbA1c test?
Do I need to change my diet or medicine?

normal.means: Your fasting blood sugar is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my blood sugar be checked?

PPBS.measures: Post-prandial glucose is your blood sugar about two hours after a meal.

low.means: Your after-meal blood sugar is below the range.
ask: Do my diabetes medicines need changing?

high.means: Your after-meal blood sugar is above the range. Your body is slow to bring sugar down after eating.
causes: The body not using insulin well
A large meal high in sugar or starch
ask: Should I have an HbA1c test?
Which foods raise my sugar the most?

normal.means: Your after-meal blood sugar is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my blood sugar be checked?

EAG.measures: Estimated average glucose turns your HbA1c into a blood sugar number, like one you would see on a home meter.

low.means: Your estimated average sugar is below the range.
causes: Same causes as a low HbA1c
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your estimated average sugar is above the recommended level.
causes: Blood sugar that has stayed high for months
ask: What average sugar should I aim for?

normal.means: Your estimated average sugar is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my HbA1c be checked?

VITD.measures: Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium and keep bones and muscles strong. Your skin makes it in sunlight.

low.means: Your vitamin D is below the range. This is very common in India. Low levels over time can weaken bones and muscles.
causes: Covering most of the skin outdoors
Darker skin, which makes vitamin D more slowly
Age, since older skin makes less
ask: Do I need a vitamin D supplement, and what dose?
How long should I take it before retesting?
Should my calcium also be checked?

high.means: Your vitamin D is above the range. This almost always comes from supplements.
causes: Taking high-dose vitamin D for a long time
ask: Should I stop or reduce my vitamin D supplement?
Should my calcium be checked?

normal.means: Your vitamin D is within the normal range on your report.
ask: Should I keep taking any supplement I am on?

B12.measures: Vitamin B12 helps make red blood cells and keeps nerves working well. It comes mostly from animal foods like milk, curd, eggs and meat.

low.means: Your vitamin B12 is below the range. Low B12 over time can cause tiredness, tingling in hands and feet, and memory problems.
causes: A vegetarian diet with little milk or curd
The stomach absorbing less B12 with age
Some medicines, such as metformin or acid-reducing tablets
ask: Do I need B12 tablets or injections?
Could my diabetes or acidity medicine be lowering my B12?
When should I retest?

high.means: Your vitamin B12 is above the range. This usually comes from supplements or injections.
ask: Should I reduce my B12 supplement?

normal.means: Your vitamin B12 is within the normal range on your report.
ask: Should I keep taking any supplement I am on?

FERR.measures: Ferritin shows how much iron your body has stored for later use.

low.means: Your ferritin is below the range. Your body's iron stores are low. This often comes before or along with low haemoglobin.
causes: Not enough iron in the diet
Blood loss, such as heavy periods or bleeding in the gut
ask: Why might my iron stores be low?
Do I need iron tablets or an iron drip?
Should I be checked for blood loss from the gut?
When should I retest?

high.means: Your ferritin is above the range. Ferritin rises with inflammation, not only with extra iron.
ask: Is this from inflammation or extra iron?
Do I need more iron tests?

normal.means: Your ferritin is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my haemoglobin?

IRON.measures: Serum iron is the amount of iron moving in your blood right now.

low.means: Your blood iron is below the range.
ask: Do I need iron tablets?

high.means: Your blood iron is above the range.
ask: Should I stop iron tablets before retesting?

normal.means: Your blood iron is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my ferritin?

TIBC.measures: TIBC shows how much iron your blood could carry. It usually goes up when iron is low.

low.means: Your TIBC is below the range.
ask: How does this fit with my ferritin?

high.means: Your TIBC is above the range. Your body may be trying to grab more iron.
ask: Do I need iron tablets?

normal.means: Your TIBC is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my ferritin?

FOLATE.measures: Folate is a B vitamin needed to make red blood cells. It comes from green leafy vegetables, dals and fruit.

low.means: Your folate is below the range.
causes: Few green vegetables or dals in the diet
ask: Do I need a folic acid tablet?

high.means: Your folate is above the range. This usually comes from supplements.
ask: Should my B12 also be checked?

normal.means: Your folate is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How does this fit with my blood count?

CRP.measures: CRP is a protein the liver makes when there is inflammation in the body.

low.means: Your CRP is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your CRP is above the range. There is some inflammation in the body. The test does not show where.
ask: What could be causing inflammation?
Should this be rechecked?

normal.means: Your CRP is within the normal range on your report.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

HSCRP.measures: hs-CRP is a more sensitive CRP test. Doctors use it to look at low-level inflammation linked to heart risk.

low.means: Your hs-CRP is below the range.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your hs-CRP is above the recommended level.
ask: What does this mean for my heart risk?
Should I repeat it when I am not unwell?

normal.means: Your hs-CRP is within the recommended range on your report.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

ESR.measures: ESR measures how fast red blood cells settle in a tube. It rises with inflammation.

low.means: Your ESR is below the range. Doctors rarely act on this result on its own.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your ESR is above the range. There may be some inflammation in the body.
causes: Low haemoglobin, which can raise ESR
ask: What could be causing this?
Should this be rechecked?

normal.means: Your ESR is within the normal range on your report.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

UPROT.measures: This checks for protein in your urine. Kidneys that are working well keep most protein in the blood, so little or none should show up.

high.means: Some protein was found in your urine. A small amount can come and go, but it can also be an early sign that the kidneys are leaking protein.
causes: Hard exercise, fever or not drinking enough water
High blood sugar over many years
ask: Should I have a urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR) test?
Could my blood sugar or blood pressure be affecting my kidneys?
When should I repeat this urine test?

normal.means: No protein was found, which matches what is expected.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

UGLU.measures: This checks for sugar in your urine. Sugar spills into urine when blood sugar is high.

high.means: Sugar was found in your urine. Your blood sugar may have been high when the sample was taken.
causes: Some diabetes medicines that remove sugar through urine
ask: Should my blood sugar be checked?
Could my medicine explain this?

normal.means: No sugar was found, which matches what is expected.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

UKET.measures: Ketones are made when the body burns fat for energy instead of sugar.

high.means: Ketones were found in your urine.
causes: Not eating for a long time
ask: Should my blood sugar be checked today?

normal.means: No ketones were found, which matches what is expected.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

UBLD.measures: This checks for blood in your urine that may be too small to see.

high.means: Blood was found in your urine.
ask: Should this urine test be repeated?
Do I need a scan?

normal.means: No blood was found, which matches what is expected.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

ULEU.measures: This checks for white blood cells in the urine, a sign the body may be fighting germs there.

high.means: Signs of white blood cells were found in your urine.
causes: A sample that was not clean-catch
ask: Do I need a urine culture?

normal.means: None were found, which matches what is expected.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

UNIT.measures: Nitrite in urine can be made by some germs that cause urine infections.

high.means: Nitrite was found in your urine.
ask: Do I need a urine culture?

normal.means: No nitrite was found, which matches what is expected.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

UBIL.measures: This checks for bilirubin in the urine. It is usually not present.

high.means: Bilirubin was found in your urine.
ask: Should my liver tests be checked?

normal.means: No bilirubin was found, which matches what is expected.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

UPH.measures: Urine pH shows how acidic or alkaline your urine is.

low.means: Your urine is more acidic than usual.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your urine is more alkaline than usual.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

normal.means: Your urine pH is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?

USG.measures: Specific gravity shows how concentrated your urine is.

low.means: Your urine is more dilute than usual.
ask: Does this need any follow-up?

high.means: Your urine is more concentrated than usual.
causes: Sugar or protein in the urine
ask: Should I drink more water?

normal.means: Your urine concentration is within the normal range on your report.
ask: How often should my urine be checked?
